entries.summary: Replaced placeholder PSF with a real Arabic 8x16 font rasterised from KacstOne Bold; captured a decisive screenshot showing the phrase "salaam arabi" (salutation in Arabic) printed three times right-anchored, proving end-to-end RTL-VT rendering.
changes: Rewrote tools/rtl-vt/generate_psf2.py to build a valid PSF2 v0 header (magic 72b54a86, 256 glyphs, charsize=16, width=8, height=16) and render each glyph from a system TTF via Pillow (ASCII from DejaVu Sans Mono Bold, Arabic from KacstOne Bold).
Regenerated drivers/video/console/fonts/arab-rtl-kbd-8x16.psf (sha256 872b4612...); glyph slots for seen lam alef meem ayn ra ba ya now contain legible Arabic bitmaps.

Cleaned visual_runner_wsl.sh: suppresses kernel console output on tty1 (console=ttyS0 only, loglevel=0, quiet), regenerates the PSF deterministically each run, prints the decisive Arabic phrase three times in natural byte order, and relies on the active RTL console mode to right-anchor the phrase.
Captured new decisive artifacts: rtlvt-arabic-rtl-decisive.(png|ppm) with clear right-anchored Arabic glyphs and no kernel boot noise.
next_focus: Polish glyph legibility further (explore 16x16 or VGA 9x16 variant).
Extend decisive proof with a longer meaningful Arabic sentence.
Port the patch-preview kernel guard through a compile-time switch without altering vt.c directly.

entries.summary: First captured Arabic RTL screenshot with placeholder PSF; superseded by real Arabic font release.
